normalization_notes.note: All figures presented in TRY millions. No USD/EUR conversion required; revenues and costs primarily TRY-based with USD crude oil procurement hedged through margin mechanisms.
Input source uses TRY millions throughout; no thousands-to-millions conversion required.

TUPRS operates under TFRS 17 (Turkish equivalent of IFRS) with IAS 29 hyperinflation revaluation active through 2024, suspended 2025 onward. This creates year-to-year comparability challenges: Equity line items (especially retained earnings and OCI) inflated by ~210B TRY (2025) from revaluation. Balance sheet structural soundness (debt repayment, asset quality) NOT affected; metrics interpretation requires separate 'adjusted' presentation excluding IAS 29 inflation adjustments.

Net refinery margin declined from ~19 $/bbl (2022) → 7.0 $/bbl (2025). This single variable drives FAVÖK by ~5–6 B TRY per $/bbl. 2026 recovery to 8–9 $/bbl is consensus target; geopolitical risk (US-Iran tensions, Hurmuz normalcy) is primary near-term catalyst.

2025 dividend: 29.3B TRY (12.93 TRY net/share); paid in two tranches (2025-03-28 = 51.19%, 2025-09-30 = 48.81%). 2026 dividend proposed: 33B TRY (14.56 TRY net/share); reflects confidence in margin recovery. Dividend coverage via FCF ~36–42B TRY annually is healthy.

20% TL depreciation vs USD → ~10–15B TRY FAVÖK headwind (partially offset by higher crude input costs in USD terms; net effect complex). Pompa fiyatı (pump price) indexation provides some protection, but margin compression in weak TRY environments is structural risk.

2024 → 2025 year-on-year: Revenue +2.5% (nominal), EBITDA +22.3% (absolute margin recovery), Net Income +63.4% (recovery from 2024 trough). No material restatements detected in disclosed comparatives.

TUPRS earnings are highly leveraged to global refinery crack spreads. 1 $/bbl change → 5–6B TRY FAVÖK impact. Current margin (7.0 $/bbl) is cyclical trough; recovery to 8–9 $/bbl is critical for 2026 consensus. Geopolitical shock (Hurmuz closure) would compress margins further.

2025 dividend 29.3B TRY, 2026 guidance 33B TRY (14.56 TRY/share). FCF of ~36–42B TRY covers these payments; however, if refinery margin stays <6 $/bbl, FCF compression could limit future distributions.

Koç Holding sold 40M shares (26 Mar 2026) at 233 TL, raising 9.32B TRY; Koç stake reduced to 50.7% (maintains control, but signals partial portfolio rebalancing). Free float increased from 46.8% → 48.9%; potentially favorable for index inclusion and foreign investor liquidity.

   - Other comprehensive income (FX translation, actuarial gains)
   - Proposed/paid dividends reconciliation

2. Complete income statement with detail:
   - Finance income (interest, dividends, FX gains itemized)
   - Finance costs (interest by instrument type, FX losses)
   - Tax expense (current and deferred breakdown)
   - Earnings per share (basic and diluted)

3. Notes to financial statements (selected sections):
   - Debt schedule (maturity profile, interest rates)
   - Derivative instruments (hedging positions)
   - Related-party transactions (intercompany)
   - Contingent liabilities (environmental, legal)
   - Accounting policies (inventory method, depreciation schedules)

4. Cash flow statement detail (operating section):
   - Working capital movements (A/R, Inventory, A/P breakdown)
   - Non-cash items (D&A, provisions, deferred taxes)
